intuition.title: Solvent and assembly
intuition.text: The reported Method 1 hexane and toluene branches produce distinct superlattice sizes and orientations; keep their product samples separate.

intuition.title: Free triphenylphosphine
intuition.text: Acetone-washed and PPh3-readded branches differ in observed film versus faceted superlattice outcomes. Figure 9 also changes deposition method, so it is not an isolated PPh3 effect.

intuition.title: What the model contributes
intuition.text: Figure 8 presents calculated interaction potentials. Its curves do not establish a measured sample structure or a source-reported atomic coordinate set.

scopeLabel: Independent scoped quick audit: all 10 main pages and Figures 1–10; SI Table S1 p.1 only. Upstream ref 45 Ag-core reduction and remaining SI are outside this accepted record.

sourceAudit.scope: Main pp.1–10; Figures 1–10; SI Table S1 p.1; upstream cited method and remaining SI excluded.

conflictPairs.text: Figure 3 Results prose says C10Ag5nm in toluene, but Figure 3 caption says 5 nm dodecanethiol-coated (C12) Ag NCs.

Figure 9 wash/readdition comparison uses Method 1 versus stated Method 2, so deposition method is a confounder; Figure 10 prose says Method 1, but its caption describes anticapillary tweezers (Method 2).
Figure 10 Results prose calls EDS area 2 Figure 9C, while Figure 10 image/caption place it in Figure 10C.
SI Table S1 ligand amount heading is printed as mL for 500/1000, inconsistent with practical interpretation; no correction asserted.

Unresolved LCEM solvent-scope conflict: Experimental Methods p.3 / printed p.4382 names toluene and a toluene/hexane mixture, whereas Results p.5 / printed p.4384 and the Figure 5 caption p.6 / printed p.4385 assign the Figure 5 C12Ag6nm observation to pure hexane. Figure 5 remains source-linked to hexane; no separate pure-toluene measured outcome is inferred.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications

general_background.title: Ligands in solution and at surfaces
general_background.summary: Ligands can associate with dissolved species and particle surfaces, affecting their interactions with the surrounding liquid. A ligand shell compatible with the solvent can provide a barrier to close particle approach, helping a dispersion resist aggregation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
